bullets: US futures and Asian shares rose Nov 18 after Nvidia's strong forecast eased AI-trade jitters; S&P futures +0.8%, Nasdaq futures +1.4%.
European stocks had their worst session since March on Nov 17: Stoxx 600 -1.8%, DAX -2.1%, FTSE -1.8%, signaling lingering risk-off.
WTI crude fell near $83.78 (-1%) on supply-surplus expectations, even with continued Middle East energy-infrastructure attacks.
10-year Treasury yield near 5.11% with hawkish Fed commentary (Musalem flagged possible further hikes), keeping rate pressure elevated.

ACN.why: Drop tied to AI-driven pricing pressure hitting IT-services peers broadly (Deloitte, Capgemini, TCS also cited), not an ACN-only issue. No analyst downgrade in dd.moves, rvol normal.
ACN.bull: Revenue per person rose and 400+ clients started AI work this year despite pricing noise.
ACN.bear: AI is structurally deflating consulting pricing and deal sizes across the sector, pressuring margins.

RVTY.why: Fell despite a Q3 beat and raised FY guidance (revenue $2.86B, EPS ~$5.43); drivers cited are valuation (66x P/E vs 36x 5yr median) and technical weakness, not business damage.
RVTY.bull: Fundamentals beat and guidance was raised; pullback looks like valuation/technical, not business damage.
RVTY.bear: Stock broke below its 50-day moving average and trades at a rich premium to fair value.

CCL.why: Decline tracks a broader cruise/travel pullback on fuel-cost and balance-sheet caution; peer Viking got a double upgrade this week ('worst could be over'), suggesting sector-wide, not CCL-specific, damage.
CCL.bull: Peer Viking's double upgrade suggests the cruise-sector selloff may be overdone and reversing.
CCL.bear: Rising fuel costs and balance-sheet/financing caution remain live concerns across cruise names.

DAL.why: Nov 13 FAA ground stop hit all major US airlines (~$345M industry pretax cost estimate), a regulatory/operational event, not DAL-specific damage. UBS raised DAL to Buy. Risk: Thanksgiving travel week falls inside the hold window.
DAL.bull: UBS upgraded DAL to Buy (PT $113) and Delta recovered faster than peers from the ground stop (5% cancellations vs 22-28%).
DAL.bear: Thanksgiving travel-week disruption risk remains elevated right after a billion-dollar industry-wide ground stop.
DAL.catalysts: Thanksgiving holiday travel week (within hold window) - upside demand but also disruption risk

EL.why: Fell despite a Q1 FY27 beat and a raised outlook plus new FY2030 targets; drop attributed to valuation (P/E 210x vs 66x 5yr median), not business damage. A mid-level exec left to become Capri's CEO (minor talent loss).
EL.bull: Fiscal Q1 beat, raised full-year outlook, and new FY2030 margin targets show the business is healthy.
EL.bear: Stock trades far above historical valuation norms, leaving it vulnerable to multiple compression.
EL.catalysts: holiday shopping season begins within hold window (demand read-through for beauty retail)

RGLD.why: Nov 12 drop hit all 22 large-cap gold peers with no company-specific news or filing from RGLD that session - broad gold-sector selloff, not company damage. Company just raised its dividend for the 26th straight year.
RGLD.bull: No company-specific bad news found; 26th consecutive annual dividend hike signals balance-sheet strength.
RGLD.bear: Royalty/streaming revenue still tracks gold-price swings, so further bullion weakness would hurt regardless of fundamentals.
RGLD.catalysts: Nov 24 Renmark investor roadshow (within hold window)

KD.why: Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3.3% YoY (EPS beat but top line weak), and the stock underperformed peers on growth concerns; analyst consensus skews Hold/Reduce. This is company-specific fundamental weakness, not sector/macro.
KD.bull: EPS beat estimates and management reaffirmed $1B+ free cash flow target despite the revenue dip.
KD.bear: Revenue is still shrinking YoY and analyst consensus is mostly Hold/Reduce on the growth outlook.

BIO.why: Q3 earnings beat but the company reaffirmed a weak FY2026 revenue outlook of -3% to +0.5% organic growth; investor concern is the growth trajectory, a company-specific issue with no evidence peers fell in sympathy.
BIO.bull: Earnings and profitability came in ahead of estimates, and Q3 constant-currency revenue growth turned positive for the first time this year.
BIO.bear: Reaffirmed FY guidance still implies flat-to-negative revenue growth for 2026, disappointing investors looking for topline momentum.

FLS.why: On Nov 3/11 FLS cut full-year organic sales guidance to -2.5%/-1.5% citing Middle East-driven delays (~$100M aftermarket hit), a company-specific guidance cut even though it later raised the low end of EPS guidance and reaffirmed its 2030 margin goal (Nov 16) on a record backlog.
FLS.bull: Record backlog and a reaffirmed 2030 margin goal, plus a new $274M institutional (Wellington) position, suggest the cut is already being absorbed.
FLS.bear: Full-year sales guidance was explicitly lowered due to Middle East-driven delays, a direct company-specific earnings-outlook cut.

HALO.why: Morgan Stanley (Nov 11, to Equal-Weight) and Leerink (Nov 7, to Market Perform) both downgraded HALO specifically over royalty step-down risk on J&J's Darzalex SC starting 2029 - a company-specific analyst call per dd.moves, not a sector move.
HALO.bull: Citizens and Evercore reiterated bullish calls (PT $149/$125) on ENHANZE approval and new ADC pipeline (Hypercon) offsetting the step-down.
HALO.bear: Two analysts downgraded specifically on durability of the royalty portfolio once Darzalex step-downs begin in 2029.
